text: {"cases":[{"id":"C01","status":"conflict","pairs":[["C01-A","C01-R1"]],"reason":"C01-A states the 2023 global anomaly was about 1.2 °C above 1951–1980 (about 2.1 °F). C01-R1 describes the same NASA 2023 analysis and 1951–1980 baseline but reports 2.1 °C, claiming it is Celsius not Fahrenheit. Same metric, baseline, and period, but values in the same unit cannot both hold; this is a summary-unit error, not a valid conversion."},{"id":"C04","status":"conflict","pairs":[["C04-A","C04-R6"]],"reason":"Both describe the same final audit of batch B17 with the same 37 included units and no exclusions. C04-A says all 37 passed with zero failures, while C04-R6 says unit B17-09 failed. These statements are directly incompatible."},{"id":"C09","status":"compatible","pairs":[],"reason":"C09-A reports 32 °F at the single T3 checkpoint. C09-R1 reports 0 °C for the same checkpoint and sample as a conversion of that Fahrenheit value. 32 °F = 0 °C is a valid unit conversion, so the two statements are compatible."},{"id":"C02","status":"conflict","pairs":[["C02-A","C02-R5"]],"reason":"Both concern release Orion 4.2 under its default configuration with no exception. C02-A says unsigned extensions are not permitted to execute, while C02-R5 says they are permitted. These cannot both hold."},{"id":"C03","status":"conflict","pairs":[["C03-A","C03-R3"]],"reason":"Both state the final settled total refund (not an installment) for invoice INV-204 on 2025-02-18, including all adjustments. C03-A gives USD 138.00 and C03-R3 gives USD 183.00, which are incompatible amounts for the same entity, date, and metric."},{"id":"C10","status":"compatible","pairs":[],"reason":"C10-A reports a rise from 8% to 10%, i.e., 2 percentage points. C10-R1 says the same change is a 25% relative increase computed from the 8% base. These are different but valid measures of the same change, so they are compatible."},{"id":"C07","status":"compatible","pairs":[],"reason":"C07-A reports the NASA 2023 anomaly of about 1.2 °C above the 1951–1980 baseline. C07-R1 reports the NOAA 2023 anomaly of 1.18 °C above the 20th-century reference average. The sources and reference periods differ, so the near-equal values do not contradict each other."},{"id":"C05","status":"conflict","pairs":[["C05-A","C05-R5"]],"reason":"Both apply to rule R5 effective 2025-06-01 and to an applicant exactly 18 on the filing date who meets the other requirements. C05-A says that applicant is eligible; C05-R5 says that applicant is ineligible because eligibility must be strictly above 18. These are incompatible."},{"id":"C08","status":"compatible","pairs":[],"reason":"C08-A gives the North branch completed-refund count for March 2025 (138). C08-R1 gives it for April 2025 (183). The periods differ, so the differing counts are not in conflict."},{"id":"C12","status":"insufficient","pairs":[],"reason":"C12-A reports 1,000 completed responses for June 2025 from first-time customers, survey S9. C12-R1 reports 2,000 completed responses for June 2025 but does not identify the survey version or the respondent population. Whether the two figures cover the same population cannot be determined, so the case cannot be decided."},{"id":"C06","status":"conflict","pairs":[["C06-A","C06-R5"]],"reason":"Both describe signed FINAL revision 3 of report Q7 for month April 2025 and region North. C06-A says revision 3 records exactly 420 completed jobs, while C06-R5 says revision 3 records exactly 390, the value that C06-A assigns to the superseded revision 2. Same revision, so the two statements are incompatible."},{"id":"C11","status":"insufficient","pairs":[],"reason":"C11-A gives a 10% March 2025 refund rate for the North branch. C11-R1 gives a 12% rate for the North branch but does not specify the period. Since the periods cannot be shown to be the same, the differing rates cannot be judged incompatible."}]}
